speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; please describe your episodic cough and shortness of breath in detail, including how long this has been happening and what triggers it. To start our evaluation, have you noticed any specific patterns, such as symptoms worsening at night or after exercise?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. You mentioned symptoms 8 weeks ago included fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion; did those symptoms eventually resolve, and do you have any history of asthma or allergies? Additionally, have you noticed wheezing when you breathe in or out?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-viral cough hypersensitivity syndrome.

The recent upper respiratory infection likely triggered a prolonged hypersensitive cough reflex that persists even after the infection has resolved. Given your age and the specific pattern of symptoms worsening at night and with exertion, this is highly consistent with this condition.
